recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The core source already satisfies FHIR-7543 when read with the later approved :iterate terminology, and reverting to :recurse would conflict with FHIR-13602.
issue_request: FHIR-7543 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core-search and asked FHIR-I to decide the transitiveness of _include and _revinclude. The resolution was to define an opt-in :recurse modifier for _include/_reverseInclude, make non-recursive behavior the default, and allow servers to limit recursion depth.
initial_application: The seed issue was explicitly applied by git-svn commit fbaf29fb043878886a33392fb9a1017135ef9fed, matching the Jira comment that cites svn revision 5813. That commit added :recurse examples and server-depth-limit text to source/search.html.
additional_context: Later final issue FHIR-13602 renamed the modifier from :recurse to :iterate, corrected include examples, and clarified that include processing defaults to the initial matches only. Later issues FHIR-31939, FHIR-46101, and FHIR-46944 refined _include:iterate wording and performance guidance without reversing FHIR-7543.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/search.html states that _include and _revinclude are invoked only on the initial search results by default, that :iterate repeats the directives on included resources, that servers decide how deeply to iterate, and that iterative search is not the default behavior.
